- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; slightly increase early forecast values, especially if recent history shows volatility.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to over-forecasting in 3–7 day horizon; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizon: if forecast is >2.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast instability: if sentiment shifts >0.5 in 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect reduced confidence, especially in 1–5 day horizon.
- Model underperforms in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67); use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean to anchor long-term forecast.
